text: 再封闭的地方当中就很难逃脱出信息茧房里
en: It is hard to escape the information cocoon in an even more closed place.

text: 尝试性的去看不同观点的文章以及分析，看看别人怎么说，以你的知识储备水平去分析这样的行为合理不合理。
en: Try reading articles and analyses from different viewpoints, see what others say, and use your own knowledge reserves to analyse whether such behaviour is reasonable or not.

text: 多动手去搜索，不要什么都听别人跟你说，这样你的信息渠道就来自于别人给你提供的而不是你自己。
en: Search more with your own hands; don't listen to everything others tell you — otherwise your information channels come from what others provide you, not from yourself.

text: 对比很重要，还有就是常识性的思维，多用多种不同角度的人称去思考，尽可能的忘记自己，试图的以他人的角度去想，在宏观点就是能够尝试着像观看电视一样带入读者看者的身份去看就会有不一样的收获。
en: Comparison is important, and so is common-sense thinking. Think from multiple different personal perspectives as much as possible; forget yourself as much as possible, and try to think from others' perspectives. At a macro level, trying to watch like a television viewer, taking on the identity of a reader or viewer, will bring different gains.

text: 多去看一些推理类的书籍或者逻辑学，没有一定的知识储备量你以为的觉醒，实际上是别人给你挖的一个更大的坑。
en: Read more reasoning books or logic. Without a certain reserve of knowledge, what you think is awakening is actually a bigger pit someone else has dug for you.

text: 同时一定要保持一个思想，那就是个人利益至上，你得利益高于一切，只有持有这个观点，你才不会被集体性的思维所洗脑。
en: At the same time, you must maintain one thought: personal interest comes first. Your interests are above all else. Only by holding this view will you not be brainwashed by collective thinking.

text: 逻辑是保持清醒的唯一的思考方法，多问几个为什么，一切如梦幻泡影。
en: Logic is the only way of thinking that keeps you awake. Ask a few more 'whys', and everything is like a dream, an illusion, a bubble, a shadow.

text: 语言是知识的钥匙
en: Language is the key to knowledge.

text: 学英语，日语，德语，西班牙语
en: Learn English, Japanese, German, Spanish.

text: 互联网链接世界 到墙外看一下看
en: The internet connects the world — go look outside the wall.

text: 中文主流社交平台也全都逛一遍
en: Browse all the mainstream Chinese social platforms too.

text: 各种专业书读一下
en: Read various professional books.

text: 跳槽各行各业试一下
en: Try switching jobs across all walks of life.

text: 信息的真实性要各个信息来源相互验证
en: Verify the authenticity of information across information sources.

text: 多看历史，要连着看，
en: Read more history, and read it continuously.

text: 和不同思想阶层的人聊天
en: Chat with people from different ideological strata.

text: 真正的大师永远怀着一颗学徒的心
en: A true master always keeps an apprentice's heart.

text: 爱你的人会骗你，怕你的人会骗你，有求于你得人会骗你！
en: People who love you will deceive you, people who fear you will deceive you, people who want something from you will deceive you!

text: 这是春秋战国时期就总结出的道理！
en: This is a truth summed up as early as the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods!

text: “信息茧房”这个说法，正在从学术研究快速走向日常生活。
en: The term 'information cocoon' is rapidly moving from academic research into everyday life.

text: 比如有年轻人吐槽“你们看过爸妈的手机吗？
en: For example, when young people complain, 'Have you seen your parents' phones?

text: 他们刷到的内容和我完全不一样，这简直就是信息茧房”时，这类说法其实混淆了“信息茧房”和“个性化推荐”概念。
en: The content they scroll to is completely different from mine — this is simply an information cocoon' — such statements actually confuse the concepts of 'information cocoon' and 'personalised recommendation'.

text: 当人们使用个性化推荐，因个人兴趣、场景等因素而得到不同的推荐结果，其实是很正常的，但将千人千面的推荐效果等同于信息茧房，有失偏颇，容易导致信息茧房概念的泛化与滥用。
en: When people use personalised recommendations and get different recommendation results due to personal interests, scenarios and other factors, it is actually quite normal. But equating the 'thousands of people, thousands of faces' recommendation effect with information cocoons is biased, and easily leads to the generalisation and abuse of the information cocoon concept.

text: 这种近乎直觉式的推断，让人喜忧参半。
en: This almost intuitive inference is bittersweet.

text: 喜的是，人们对新技术的社会影响保持了认知上的敏感和反思。
en: The good news is that people remain cognitively sensitive to and reflective about the social impact of new technologies.

text: 忧的是，信息茧房概念逐渐泛化，陷入了过于简单化的归因，对算法技术的评判有失公允，并且有可能滑向不利于社会创新的技术悲观论调。
en: The worrying part is that the information cocoon concept is gradually becoming generalised, falling into overly simplistic attribution, making unfair judgments about algorithm technology, and possibly sliding into techno-pessimistic rhetoric unfavourable to social innovation.

text: 信息茧房这个术语有两层含义。
en: The term information cocoon has two layers of meaning.

text: 首先，这个词语描述了个人所感知的同质化信息环境。
en: First, this term describes the homogeneous information environment perceived by individuals.

text: 早在2006年，美国政治学家、法学家卡斯·桑斯坦在《信息乌托邦》（Infotopia: How Many Minds Produce Knowledge）一书中，用“茧房”来比喻这样一个环境：因为个性化的信息过滤，个体只能接受到符合自己观点的信息，因此陷入到了一个同质化的信息环境中。
en: As early as 2006, American political scientist and jurist Cass Sunstein, in Information Utopia (Infotopia: How Many Minds Produce Knowledge), used 'cocoon' as a metaphor for such an environment: because of personalised information filtering, individuals can only receive information consistent with their own views, and thus fall into a homogeneous information environment.

text: 其次，在学术研究中，过滤泡、回声室是比信息茧房更常用的概念。
en: Second, in academic research, filter bubbles and echo chambers are more commonly used concepts than information cocoons.

text: 人们上网时都有类似的体验，立场不同的双方就某个争议话题展开论战，结果不仅谁也说服不了谁、谁也不愿意理解谁，甚至还会加强自己原先的立场。
en: People have similar experiences online: two sides with different stances debate a controversial topic, and the result is not only that neither can convince the other, nor is willing to understand the other, but they even strengthen their original stances.

text: 回声室就描述了这样一种状况：人们生活在一个封闭的社交圈中，同质化的信息不断重复、放大，导致回声室内的成员对外界的信息接触越来越少，而只能听到和自己一致观点的声音。
en: The echo chamber describes just such a situation: people live in a closed social circle, where homogeneous information is constantly repeated and amplified, so that members of the echo chamber come into contact with outside information less and less, and can only hear voices consistent with their own views.

text: 不过，算法和茧房的因果关系也未经证实。
en: However, the causal relationship between algorithms and cocoons is also unproven.

text: 《打破社交媒体棱镜》一书中，美国杜克大学政治学与公共政策教授克里斯·贝尔做了一个实验，当给用户提供了对立的观点时，人们反而更极端、更捍卫自己原来的立场了。
en: In Breaking the Social Media Prism, Chris Bail, professor of political science and public policy at Duke University, conducted an experiment: when users were provided with opposing views, people became more extreme and defended their original stances even more.

text: 这个实验说明，哪怕我们接触的是多样化的信息，仍然会拥护自己的立场，甚至变得极端，这个过程并不一定需要经过“过滤泡”或“信息茧房”的中介。
en: This experiment shows that even when we come into contact with diverse information, we still uphold our own stances, and even become extreme — a process that does not necessarily require the mediation of 'filter bubbles' or 'information cocoons'.

text: 信息茧房、过滤泡、回声室等概念都描述了一个共同的担忧：在选择性的信息接触中，人们可能会陷入一种自我强化的反馈循环，从而失去了接触多种信息、不同观点的机会。
en: Concepts such as information cocoons, filter bubbles and echo chambers all describe a common concern: in selective information contact, people may fall into a self-reinforcing feedback loop, thereby losing opportunities to contact diverse information and different views.

text: 这个复杂的社会问题有很多成因，受到包括个体、技术、场景与社会等多种因素的共同影响。
en: This complex social problem has many causes, influenced by multiple factors including individuals, technology, scenarios and society.

text: 但是在人们的日常认知中经常把这个多因——多果的问题，简化为“算法导致信息茧房”形式的单因——单果的说法。
en: But in people's everyday cognition, this multi-cause, multi-effect problem is often simplified into a single-cause, single-effect statement in the form of 'algorithms cause information cocoons'.

text: 要弄清楚这个问题，我们需要全面地认识算法。
en: To understand this problem clearly, we need a comprehensive understanding of algorithms.

text: 首先，在技术上，算法就是计算方法。
en: First, technically, an algorithm is a calculation method.

text: 我们对数学中的鸡兔同笼问题的求解，就是最简单的计算方法。
en: Our solving of the chickens-and-rabbits-in-a-cage problem in mathematics is the simplest calculation method.

text: 推荐算法要解决的问题是随互联网而来的海量信息的分发难题。
en: The problem recommendation algorithms must solve is the distribution problem of massive information that came with the internet.

text: “猜你想看”也是一道算法题，信息平台根据人们的地理位置数据、已有浏览记录、朋友的兴趣等，完成信息的高效分发。
en: 'Guess what you'd like to see' is also an algorithm problem: information platforms complete efficient information distribution based on people's geographic location data, existing browsing records, friends' interests, and so on.

text: 推荐算法在用户和内容之间建立起有效的、符合偏好和需求的桥梁。
en: Recommendation algorithms build an effective bridge between users and content that matches preferences and needs.

text: 如果没有推荐算法，我们可能会淹没在无边无际的信息海洋中，感到迷茫和不知所措，我们无法有效地获取所需的信息，甚至可能引发更严重的问题，比如信息瘫痪和信息回避。
en: Without recommendation algorithms, we might drown in a boundless ocean of information, feeling lost and at a loss; we would be unable to effectively obtain needed information, and might even trigger more serious problems, such as information paralysis and information avoidance.

text: 因此，从全局上看，算法是服务民众需求、有利社会发展的，这一基本判断应是主流共识。
en: Therefore, from an overall perspective, algorithms serve the needs of the people and benefit social development — this basic judgment should be the mainstream consensus.

text: 其次，从市场经济角度看，提供这项服务的平台公司需要盈利，因此推荐算法还要解决留住用户，然后将用户注意力有效售卖给广告商的问题。
en: Second, from a market economy perspective, platform companies providing this service need to make a profit, so recommendation algorithms must also solve the problem of retaining users and then effectively selling user attention to advertisers.

text: 正如纪录片《监视资本主义：智能陷阱》（The Social Dilemma）中指出的，社交媒体平台和搜索引擎使用的推荐算法，根据用户的历史行为和偏好，个性化地推送信息。
en: As pointed out in the documentary The Social Dilemma, social media platforms and search engines use recommendation algorithms to push information personalised according to users' historical behaviour and preferences.

text: 平台就像商场，如果商场总提供某一类或某几类商品，无法提供更多品类的商品，消费者可能会减少使用甚至抛弃它。
en: A platform is like a shopping mall: if the mall always provides one or a few categories of goods and cannot provide more categories, consumers may use it less or even abandon it.

text: 从商业角度，平台也会通过分发多样性信息，来留存用户，而不是刻意制造茧房。
en: From a commercial perspective, platforms also retain users by distributing diverse information, rather than deliberately creating cocoons.

text: 也有研究显示，用户仍然有主观能动性，也并非一味被动接受算法的投喂。
en: Research also shows that users still have subjective initiative, and do not blindly passively accept algorithm feeding.

text: 宾夕法尼亚大学的杨天、黄圣淳等研究发现，喜欢用今日头条看娱乐信息的人，也顺便看了新闻。
en: Research by Tian Yang, Huang Shengchun and others at the University of Pennsylvania found that people who like to use Toutiao to read entertainment information also incidentally read news.

text: 也就是说，人们使用算法驱动的信息分发平台之后，并没有陷入娱乐的茧房中不可自拔，而是随着娱乐信息消费的增加，新闻信息的消费也增加。
en: That is to say, after people use algorithm-driven information distribution platforms, they do not fall into entertainment cocoons and become unable to extricate themselves; instead, as entertainment information consumption increases, news information consumption also increases.

text: 从传播的角度上讲，这个研究的结果很有意义，因为它提出了一个反常识的发现：算法平台上的消费者不仅没有娱乐至死，而是也履行着“好公民”的职责。
en: From a communication perspective, this research result is very meaningful, because it proposes a counter-intuitive discovery: consumers on algorithm platforms not only do not amuse themselves to death, but also fulfil their duties as 'good citizens'.

text: 此外，从技术哲学的视角，技术与社会相互建构。
en: In addition, from the perspective of philosophy of technology, technology and society mutually construct each other.

text: 推荐算法并不是一个完全独立的存在，而是与多种社会因素相互交织、共同发展的结果。
en: Recommendation algorithms are not a completely independent existence, but the result of intertwining and co-developing with various social factors.

text: 它根据我们的个人兴趣来推荐信息，但也受到政府、公司、用户等多种社会因素共同影响，进而产生了“千人千面”的推荐效果。
en: They recommend information according to our personal interests, but are also jointly influenced by governments, companies, users and other social factors, thereby producing the 'thousands of people, thousands of faces' recommendation effect.

text: 而当我们搞清楚了何为算法、何为茧房，我们也就可以理解为什么算法成了信息茧房的替罪羊。
en: And when we understand what algorithms are and what cocoons are, we can also understand why algorithms have become the scapegoat for information cocoons.

text: 第一，这个替罪羊现象是大众认知仓促简化的结果。
en: First, this scapegoat phenomenon is the result of hasty simplification of mass cognition.

text: 算法技术深度嵌入日常生活后，和各样社会问题产生了复杂的勾连。
en: After algorithm technology became deeply embedded in daily life, it became intricately linked with various social problems.

text: 但人们并没有时间、或没有心力去进行明辨，就想要寻求一个易懂的、易交流的说法，来描述这种“千人千面”的信息体验，却找不到除茧房、过滤泡这类比喻之外的词汇。
en: But people do not have the time, or do not have the energy, to distinguish clearly, and want to seek an easy-to-understand, easy-to-communicate statement to describe this 'thousands of people, thousands of faces' information experience, yet cannot find vocabulary other than metaphors like cocoons and filter bubbles.

text: 于是，在大众讨论中，信息茧房的概念被挪用和滥用，相应地，概念语义也出现了泛化。
en: Thus, in public discussion, the information cocoon concept has been appropriated and abused, and accordingly, the concept's semantics have also become generalised.

text: 把对信息茧房、沟通困难等的担忧，都仓促地挪用到了推荐算法上。
en: Concerns about information cocoons, communication difficulties, etc., have all been hastily appropriated to recommendation algorithms.

text: 如果人们不愿意充分全面地去认知算法的原理，信息茧房的含义，就匆匆地将信息茧房完全归咎于算法，也是有失公允的。
en: If people are unwilling to fully and comprehensively understand the principles of algorithms, hastily attributing the meaning of information cocoons entirely to algorithms is also unfair.

text: 第二，正如社会心理学的“替罪羊理论”所说，人们往往会把负面体验归因于外群体。
en: Second, as social psychology's 'scapegoat theory' says, people often attribute negative experiences to out-groups.

text: 在这里，人们把社会问题归因于技术。
en: Here, people attribute social problems to technology.

text: 人们如果在现实生活中意义感缺失，更倾向在信息流中花费更多时间，放下手机后，人们就容易将自己的空虚感归因到算法身上。
en: If people lack a sense of meaning in real life, they are more inclined to spend more time in information streams; after putting down their phones, people easily attribute their sense of emptiness to algorithms.

text: 心理学家戈登·W·阿尔波特的“替罪羊理论”（scapegoat theory）提出，当人们经受负面的情绪时，会倾向于把这种感受去归咎于另一个群体或个人。
en: Psychologist Gordon W. Allport's 'scapegoat theory' proposes that when people experience negative emotions, they tend to attribute such feelings to another group or individual.

text: 如果让算法作为信息茧房的背锅侠，蕴含了一个前提：用户是被动的，没有主动性的，技术为刀俎，网民为鱼肉。
en: Making algorithms the scapegoat for information cocoons implies a premise: users are passive, without initiative; technology is the knife and chopping block, and netizens are the meat on the block.

text: 但实际上，推荐算法在技术上也给用户的兴趣赋予了很多能动性。
en: But in fact, recommendation algorithms technically also give users' interests a lot of initiative.

text: 如果用户对京剧感兴趣，在京剧类型内容上停留时间长，就会得到更多的推送。
en: If a user is interested in Peking opera and stays long on Peking opera content, they will get more pushes.

text: 其实，就算是没有算法的时代里，人们也会不同程度地生活在自己构建的同质化信息圈中。
en: In fact, even in an era without algorithms, people would live to varying degrees in homogeneous information circles they built themselves.

text: 报刊时代，也有人只看社会新闻；电视时代，也有人只看体育频道。
en: In the newspaper era, some people only read social news; in the television era, some people only watched sports channels.

text: 但人们并没有把这种单一化、同质化的信息消费归咎于报刊和电视。
en: But people did not attribute this single, homogeneous information consumption to newspapers and television.

text: 真正能打破信息茧房的，并不是对一个传播技术的讨伐和绞杀，而是对受众或用户的信息素养、社会公共信息生态治理等等多方面能力的考验。
en: What can truly break information cocoons is not the condemnation and strangulation of a communication technology, but a test of many capabilities such as the information literacy of audiences or users, and the governance of the social public information ecology.

text: 可见，面对复杂的社会问题时，人们总会想寻找一个简化易懂的说法。
en: It can be seen that when facing complex social problems, people always want to find a simplified, easy-to-understand statement.

text: 这个替罪羊可能是另一群人，也可能是技术，而“信息茧房”就成为了信息同质化、娱乐至死、意义虚无等复杂社会症候的简化替罪羊。
en: This scapegoat may be another group of people, or it may be technology, and 'information cocoon' has become a simplified scapegoat for complex social symptoms such as information homogenisation, amusing ourselves to death, and meaninglessness.

text: 第三，纵观媒介发展史，算法既不是第一只为负面情绪赎罪的替罪羊，也不会是最后一位替社会问题挡枪的背锅侠。
en: Third, looking at the history of media development, algorithms are neither the first scapegoat to atone for negative emotions, nor will they be the last to take the bullet for social problems.

text: 新兴的传播技术带来的变革如果超出了人们能够驾驭的范围，就很容易成为更广泛问题归咎对象。
en: When changes brought by emerging communication technologies exceed the range people can handle, they easily become the object of blame for broader problems.

text: 例如，柏拉图在《菲德罗篇》中猛烈批评“文字”这种当时的新技术，认为它破坏了口头交流增长智慧的方式。
en: For example, Plato fiercely criticised 'writing', the new technology of the time, in Phaedrus, believing it destroyed the way oral communication grows wisdom.

text: 清朝末年，被喻为“顺风耳”的电报技术传入当时面对内忧外患的清朝，电报本可以用于提高军事情报的传递效率，但也遭到了很多大臣的反对。
en: At the end of the Qing dynasty, telegraph technology, likened to 'clairaudient ears', was introduced to the Qing dynasty facing internal troubles and external threats. Telegraphs could have been used to improve the transmission efficiency of military intelligence, but they were opposed by many ministers.

text: 其中一位名叫崇厚的大臣认为，这种新技术“贻害无穷”，因为电报杆插得太深，可能破坏风水，吸走大清的地气。
en: One minister named Chonghou believed this new technology was 'endlessly harmful', because telegraph poles inserted too deeply might destroy feng shui and drain the Qing dynasty's earth energy.

text: 21世纪初，网络游戏一度成了“网瘾”的替罪羊。
en: At the beginning of the 21st century, online games once became the scapegoat for 'internet addiction'.

text: 当网络上的喷子太多，我们又武断地抓出社交媒体来做祸首。
en: When there are too many trolls online, we arbitrarily grab social media as the culprit.

text: 如今，人们又捉住了算法和大数据，作为信息同质化和观点极化的替罪羊。
en: Today, people have caught algorithms and big data as scapegoats for information homogenisation and opinion polarisation.

text: 认识到这个算法是替罪羊现象，克制地使用简化归因，对个人和社会都是有益的。
en: Recognising this algorithm-as-scapegoat phenomenon and restraining the use of simplified attribution is beneficial to both individuals and society.

text: 对个人而言，我们应该有意识地培养自己的自控力，为自己设计更加健康的信息套餐，运用科学和积极的思维来使用算法。
en: For individuals, we should consciously cultivate our self-control, design healthier information packages for ourselves, and use algorithms with scientific and positive thinking.

text: 例如，通过算法推荐，用户找到了独特品味的图书、小众出版商也觅得了投缘的小众读者群。
en: For example, through algorithm recommendations, users found books of unique taste, and niche publishers also found congenial niche reader groups.

text: 对社会来说，我们保持开放包容的心态，才能在社会认知上为新技术创新作好准备，助力孵化更多的创意产品来方便我们的生活，而代际沟通困难、意义虚无、错失焦虑、意见极化等结构性的社会问题，也不能把责任简单推到用户或技术身上，还需要通过系统设计思维，推动全社会一起来改善
en: For society, maintaining an open and inclusive mindset is what prepares social cognition for new technological innovation, helping incubate more creative products to make our lives convenient, while structural social problems such as intergenerational communication difficulties, meaninglessness, fear of missing out, and opinion polarisation cannot simply have their responsibility pushed onto users or technology — they also need systematic design thinking to push the whole society to improve together
